title: Seller Empathy Sprint — Pilot Enablement & Battle Brief (Iter 0)
summary: A compact, speaker-noted enablement deck + persona battlecards to run a 2-week 'Empathy Sprint' pilot. Focus: fast technical discovery, ops confidence checks, and scripted responses to common objections during pilot windows.
body:
Slide 1 — Title: Seller Empathy Sprint: Pilot Enablement & Battle Brief (Iter 0)
Speaker notes: Quick intro. Purpose: help SEs run a short pilot that surfaces operational constraints and builds buyer trust. Not a product deep-dive; it's an ops-first checklist + persona battlecards. Recommended runtime: 10–20 min for initial kickoff, 1–2 quick followups during pilot.

Slide 2 — Why an Empathy Sprint?
- Problem: pilots stall because platform teams fear unknowns (latency spikes, cost blowouts, compliance risk).
- Hypothesis: a short, repeatable discovery + test plan that answers "can we run this reliably" reduces friction and shortens time-to-value.
- Goal: land a pilot commit with clear SLOs and an agree-upon rollback/fallback plan.
Speaker notes: Frame this as risk-reduction for the customer. Use "we'll prove it in two weeks" language.

Slide 3 — Sprint Anatomy (2-week example)
- Day 0: Kickoff (10–20 min) — align personas, objectives, success metric (latency p95, throughput TPS, cost per 1k tokens, security/region).
- Day 1–3: Smoke tests — small sample traffic, measure cold-start behavior, KV/prefix cache characteristics.
- Day 4–9: Load envelope and edge cases — burst tests, long-context behavior, failure injection (simulate region loss/slow disk).
- Day 10–12: Quality checks & evals — run 50–100 curated prompts, track regressions, compare quantized vs full model outputs.
- Day 13–14: Wrap & next steps — present results, propose Dedicated or routing policy adjustments.
Speaker notes: Keep every step tied to a decision. If SLOs fail, do rollback and present mitigations.

Slide 4 — Quick diagnostic checklist (ops-first)
- Network: estimate egress latency to chosen region, confirm VPC peering or proxy setup.
- Latency: sample p50/p95 for short (32 token) and long (512 token) requests. Target p95 < 250ms for interactive pilots, < 800ms for batch/async.
- Throughput: single-GPU sustained TPS and cold-start throughput under burst.
- Cost baseline: estimate cost per 1k tokens and expected monthly cost at pilot QPS. Include embedding vs generation ratio.
- Data controls: confirm KMS, retention, and log redaction settings.
- Fallback plan: routing to cheaper quantized model variant or queueing/batching.
Speaker notes: Provide quick commands (see appendix) to run the checks; results should be recorded in the pilot doc.

Slide 5 — Risk Radar & Decision Triggers
- Green: all checks within targets -> propose Dedicated or sustained hosted config.
- Yellow: intermittent p95 spikes, acceptable cost -> recommend caching/batching and extended observation.
- Red: missing data controls or regulatory blockers -> escalate to solutions + security; pause public-hosted traffic.
Speaker notes: Decision triggers are binary where possible. Push for clear acceptance criteria.

Slide 6 — Mini battlecard: Platform Engineer (Ops-focused)
Key concerns: network topology, observability, autoscale safety, data isolation.
Top-line script: "We treat your pilot as an ops experiment — we'll run controlled traffic and give you a per-route dashboard with token-level cost and latency for each test so you can see exact impact."
Metrics to show live: p95 latency, GPU utilization, per-request token cost, cache hit rate.
Common objections + quick responses:
- "We can't expose prod traffic": "Start with a synthetic replay that mirrors production traffic and use canary routing; we provide a deterministic replay scaffold and tracing hooks."
- "We need auditability": "We produce audit logs, and we can integrate with your KMS/HSM; show sample export in under 30 minutes."
- "What if latency spikes?": "We offer automatic fallback to a pinned, more-conservative model variant and region-level routing; we'll configure an on-call playbook for the pilot."
Playbook step (if blocked): open a tickets with SRE tag, attach the smoke test results (see appendix command), propose workaround: route read-only traffic to cached responses.

Slide 7 — Mini battlecard: SRE/Platform Reliability
Key concerns: burst isolation, tail-latency, fail-open vs fail-closed.
Top-line script: "We quantify tail risk during the pilot with an aggressive burst schedule and compare to your SLOs — we don't promote anything to production until your SRE signs off."
Quick tests to run:
- 5x normal burst for 2m, measure p99 and error budget burn.
- Simulate a model fallback and measure cold-start time to confirm fallback preserves latency SLAs.
Canned replies:
- "Token cost vs QoS tradeoff": Provide quick estimator: e.g., at 100 QPS with mean payload 120 tokens, expected hosted cost ~ $0.00045 per 1k tokens — convert to $/hour and show latency-cost tradeoffs.
- "We need isolation": Outline Dedicated capacity path and expected lead time (2–6 weeks depending on region & capacity).

Slide 8 — Mini battlecard: Procurement / Legal
Key concerns: pricing predictability, contract length, liability, data residency.
Top-line script: "Pilot pricing: capped run with a small overage buffer and weekly transparency. Enterprise agreements include reserved capacity discounts and enterprise SLAs."
Negotiation anchors:
- Offer a 4–8 week pilot credit cap (e.g., $5k–$25k depending on scale) with break clause if SLOs not met.
- Provide a short compliance checklist and an SOW template to accelerate legal review.

Slide 9 — Objection playbook (rapid responses)
- "Too expensive": "Let's run a cost-sim with your sample traffic for 1 week — we'll suggest batching/quantization to hit your target."
- "Latency unpredictable": "We'll run a 24-hour latency baseline and give you the 95/99 percentiles; if you need hard p95 SLA we can reserve Dedicated capacity."
- "Model quality differs": "We run paired A/B on 100 labeled prompts and surface regression alerts by category; we'll iterate model or prompt to meet your quality bar."

Slide 10 — Escalation & on-call playbook for pilots
- Level 0 (SE-led): run smoke tests, collect logs, apply caching rules.
- Level 1 (SE + Solutions Eng): implement routing change, enable quantized variant, increase autoscale burst.
- Level 2 (SRE + Infra): hardware reprovision, region failover, investigate kernel-level regressions.
- Document a clear SLA for each level (response time windows e.g., 1h, 4h, 24h).
Speaker notes: Ensure customer agrees to the escalation path at kickoff to avoid surprises.

Appendix A — Rapid commands & example outputs (copy/paste friendly)
- Smoke test: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"rwd-large-v1","input":"Hello world","max_tokens":64}'
  - Capture: elapsed_ms, tokens_generated, model_variant, region. Example result string: {elapsed_ms: 78, tokens: 34, model_variant: "rwd-large-v1", region: "us-west-2"}
- Bulk replay: python replay_traffic.py --source sample-replay.json --qps 20 --duration 300 --collect-metrics true
- Cache check: GET /pilot/cache/status returns hit_rate, prefix_hits, kv_entries
- Cost snapshot: curl https://api.redwood.example/v1/usage?snapshot=true -> returns estimated_cost_per_1k_tokens: 0.00045

Appendix B — Mini playbook templates (to share in pilot doc)
- Kickoff template: list of attendees, acceptance criteria, data controls required, tentative SLOs.
- Smoke test report template: table fields: test_id, timestamp, qps, p50, p95, errors, notes.
- Wrap report template: outcome (go/no-go), recommended next-step (Dedicated / extend pilot / stop).

Appendix C — Persona one-pagers (copy these into the pilot Google doc)
- Platform Eng one-pager: Key asks, show commands to run, three graphs to include (p95 vs QPS, cache hit rate over time, cost per 1k tokens).
- SRE one-pager: failure modes, short checklist for burst simulation, rollback checks.
- Procurement one-pager: pilot cap proposal, optional renewal discount tiers, legal checklist.

Notes for SEs (practical tips)
- Use concrete numbers: never say "it's fast" — show p95/p99 and per-token cost.
- Anchor recommendations: always propose a simple mitigation (cache, route, model variant) before recommending Dedicated.
- Keep communication scoped and scheduled: weekly sync + ad-hoc channel for incidents.

Open questions / items to iterate in next version
- Add a pre-built replay of common enterprise traffic (sales to own) for repeatable benchmarks.
- Add an automated 24h pilot report generator.
- Standardize pilot credit caps by segment.

Export checklist before sharing with customer
- Replace sample tokens with real tenant id in metrics.
- Remove any internal debug flags from commands.
- Attach a proposed SLO table and acceptance criteria.

[End of deck]

-- Battlecard extracts to paste into one-pagers for customer-facing pilot doc --

Battlecard: Platform Engineer (one-paragraph summary)
We will treat the pilot as an ops experiment. Short tests first: latency baseline (p50/p95 for 32/512 tokens), cold-start behavior, cache hit rate. If latency fails acceptably, enable prefix caching and a quantized model variant; if data controls are missing, we pause public-hosted traffic and propose VPC peering or Private deployment.

Battlecard: SRE (one-paragraph summary)
SRE care is tail risk. We'll run an aggressive burst schedule and simulate failover. If p99 degrades above your error budget, we either lower concurrency, pin to Dedicated, or add circuit-breakers at the routing layer.

Battlecard: Procurement (one-paragraph summary)
Pricing: pilot credit + weekly transparency + capped overages. Ask for budget range and propose a credit cap. Provide SOW and compliance checklist to accelerate contracting.

Checklist (first call)
- Confirm personas on call (ops, SRE, procurement).
- Agree acceptance criteria with numbers.
- Share sample traffic or replay.
- Schedule Day 3 and Day 11 syncs.

End of file.
